episodes.195030: Convection formed in the vicinity of a stationary front over South-Central Texas. Thunderstorms developed in an anomalously moist airmass with weak steering flow. This led to slow moving, heavy rain producing cells and flash flooding.
episodes.195271: A shortwave trough brushed across southern Wyoming, resulting in enough support for the development of scattered high-based thunderstorms, and isolated severe level wind gusts.
episodes.195642: Deep moisture and strong shear remained across northeast Utah and northwest Colorado as a positively tilted trough moved through northwest Colorado with drier air pushing in behind this wave. Instability in the 500 to 1000 J/kg range along with strong shear and enough moisture resulted in some strong to severe storms, one of which produced large hail in Moffatt County in addition to heavy rain.
episodes.196125: A front was stalled across NE FL with a meandering coastal low offshore of the local Atlantic coast. Above normal atmospheric moisture, warm temperatures aloft and slow storm motion produced localized heavy rainfall over a diurnally unstable airmass with waves of gusty showers moving onshore. Wind gusts with the coastal low along the local Atlantic coast increased to 40-50 mph after 8 pm on 9/3 through midnight along the Duval County FL coast.
episodes.196145: Training, slow moving bands of flooding rainfall impacted Duval county and the I-95 corridor during the morning commute with a stationary front across the area and high moisture content. Flood and urban area Flash flooding caused some structure inundation, cars to be trapped in flood water and widespread road flooding.
episodes.196472: Southeast winds in the low to mid levels over South Florida brought in plenty of moisture and instability to support the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the late morning to early afternoon hours on September 4th.
episodes.196568: An upper-level low moved across Wyoming and brought enough shear to support a landspout tornado in Sublette County, along with 2 other funnels. The tornado remained over open ground and produced no known damage. A pair of cold air funnels formed near Natrona in western Natrona County, but there was no evidence of a circulation at the ground.
episodes.196855: Ridge of high pressure allowed for high based thunderstorms to develop, some of which produced strong winds.
episodes.196890: A broad area of low pressure collocated with a stalled surface boundary along the coast provided multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms over South Texas, with greatest rainfall and flooding reports over the Coastal Bend. Rainfall amounts were observed over 8 for the event with multiple roads flooded in the Aransas Pass area.
